blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Kitchen Renovation Cost in Eltham?
blogPosts.excerpt: Planning a kitchen renovation in Eltham? Here is a realistic breakdown of costs, pricing factors and tips for getting the best value on your new kitchen.
body: The cost of a kitchen renovation in Eltham varies widely depending on the size of your kitchen, the materials you choose and the overall scope of the project. Eltham is home to a diverse mix of period homes, mid-century builds and contemporary family residences, each presenting unique renovation challenges and exciting opportunities. Whether your kitchen is in a heritage cottage near the Eltham War Memorial or a modern townhouse closer to Research, understanding typical cost ranges helps you plan with confidence. In this guide, we break down what Eltham homeowners can expect to pay for their kitchen renovation at every budget level, from simple refreshes to complete overhauls.

Several key factors influence the overall cost of your Eltham kitchen renovation. The size of your kitchen is the most obvious determinant, with larger kitchens requiring more materials and more labour hours to complete. The scope of work is equally important. A cosmetic refresh involving new paint, updated hardware and a replacement benchtop will cost significantly less than a full structural renovation that moves walls, relocates plumbing or adds an island bench. Material selection is another major variable. Natural stone benchtops like Caesarstone command a premium compared to laminate, while custom-built cabinetry costs more than pre-assembled alternatives. Additional costs to consider include plumbing and electrical upgrades, council approvals for heritage-listed properties and the expense of setting up a temporary kitchen during the renovation period.

For Eltham homeowners on a tighter budget, a kitchen refresh costing between $10,000 and $20,000 can make a surprisingly big impact. At this price point, you might choose to reface or repaint existing cabinetry rather than replace it entirely, swap out old handles for modern pulls and install a new laminate or timber-look benchtop. A fresh splashback, whether it is classic white subway tile or a simple glass panel, can also dramatically update the look of your kitchen without breaking the bank. Upgrading to energy-efficient appliances during this process adds long-term value to your Eltham home. The key to a successful budget renovation is working with an experienced team that knows how to maximise visual impact while keeping costs under control. Our Eltham showroom has plenty of affordable inspiration on display.

A mid-range kitchen renovation in Eltham typically falls between $25,000 and $45,000 and is the most popular choice among local homeowners. At this level, you can expect brand-new custom cabinetry designed to fit your exact kitchen dimensions, a quality stone benchtop such as Caesarstone or Essastone, and a stylish tile or glass splashback. New plumbing fixtures, an undermount sink and updated lighting are usually included. Many Eltham homeowners at this budget also choose to reconfigure their kitchen layout, perhaps adding a breakfast bar or island bench to improve workflow and entertaining space. This is the sweet spot where you get a kitchen that looks and feels completely new, built to last for decades, without the premium price tag of a luxury renovation. It is where most of our Eltham clients find the best balance of quality and value.

For Eltham homeowners seeking the ultimate kitchen transformation, a premium renovation starting from $50,000 and extending well beyond $80,000 offers unlimited possibilities. At this level, every element is custom-designed and built to your exact specifications. Think floor-to-ceiling cabinetry with integrated soft-close mechanisms, natural stone benchtops with waterfall edges, designer splashbacks and top-of-the-range Miele or Bosch appliances. Premium renovations often include structural changes such as removing walls to create open-plan living, adding skylights for natural light or extending the kitchen into adjacent spaces. Integrated lighting systems, pull-out pantry units and bespoke storage solutions elevate both the look and functionality of your new kitchen. While this is a significant investment, a premium kitchen renovation in Eltham adds substantial value to your property and creates a space your family will enjoy for years to come.

Beyond the headline renovation cost, Eltham homeowners should budget for several often-overlooked expenses. Setting up a temporary kitchen in another room with a microwave, kettle and portable cooktop will keep your household running during the renovation period, which typically spans six to twelve weeks for a full kitchen overhaul. If your Eltham property is heritage-listed or in a heritage overlay zone, additional council permits and approvals may be required, adding both time and cost. Unexpected issues such as outdated wiring, hidden water damage or asbestos in older homes can also surface once demolition begins, so building a contingency buffer of ten to fifteen percent into your budget is wise. The best way to avoid surprises is to work with an experienced Eltham renovation team that conducts a thorough assessment before providing a fixed, upfront quote.

blogPosts.title: Best Kitchen Layout Ideas for Eltham's Period and Modern Homes
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the best kitchen layouts for Eltham homes, from heritage cottages to modern builds. Find the perfect design to suit your space and lifestyle.
body: Choosing the right kitchen layout is one of the most important decisions you will make during your Eltham kitchen renovation. The layout determines how you move through the space, how efficiently you can prepare meals and how well the kitchen integrates with your living areas. Eltham is known for its beautiful mix of housing styles, from charming period cottages with compact kitchens to spacious modern homes with open-plan designs. Each style demands a different approach to layout planning. In this guide, we explore the most popular kitchen layouts suited to Eltham homes and help you decide which one will work best for your family's needs, your available space and your renovation budget.

The galley kitchen remains one of the most efficient layouts for Eltham's period homes and smaller houses. This design features two parallel runs of cabinetry with a walkway in between, creating a compact work triangle that puts everything within arm's reach. Galley kitchens work particularly well in Eltham's older homes along Main Street and the surrounding heritage areas where space is at a premium. Modern galley designs incorporate sleek handleless cabinetry, integrated appliances and clever pull-out storage to make the most of every centimetre. If your Eltham kitchen is narrow but long, a galley layout with cabinetry on both sides maximises storage and benchtop space without requiring structural changes. Adding open shelving on one side can create a more open, airy feel while maintaining the layout's renowned efficiency.

The L-shaped kitchen is one of the most versatile layouts for Eltham homes and works beautifully in both open-plan and enclosed kitchen spaces. This design uses two adjoining walls to create a natural work triangle between the sink, cooktop and refrigerator, keeping your kitchen workflow smooth and intuitive. For Eltham families who love to entertain, the L-shape easily accommodates a breakfast bar or dining table at the open end, creating a social hub that connects the kitchen to the living area. This layout is particularly popular in Eltham's modern townhouses and newer builds in Research and Viewbank where open-plan living is a key feature. The L-shaped design also adapts well to corner spaces, making it ideal for kitchens that sit at the junction of two rooms.

If your Eltham kitchen has the space, an island bench transforms the room into a true centrepiece of the home. Kitchen islands serve multiple purposes: they add valuable benchtop workspace, provide extra storage underneath and create a natural gathering point for family and guests. In Eltham's larger homes, particularly those in Greensborough and the leafier streets near Eltham North, an island bench with seating on one side becomes the heart of daily life, from breakfast through to evening meals. Popular island designs include waterfall stone edges, integrated sinks and cooktops, and contrasting cabinetry colours that make the island a visual focal point. When planning an island, allow at least 900mm of clearance on all sides for comfortable movement. Our Eltham showroom features several island configurations you can walk through and experience first-hand.

For Eltham homeowners with very small kitchens, a U-shaped layout or a single-wall design can deliver surprising functionality. The U-shape wraps cabinetry around three walls, creating an immersive workspace with everything within easy reach. This layout works brilliantly in Eltham's compact units and apartments where every square centimetre counts. Clever additions like a fold-down breakfast table or a pull-out benchtop extension can add flexibility without permanently consuming floor space. Alternatively, the single-wall kitchen consolidates all cabinetry, appliances and benchtops along one wall, making it perfect for studio apartments or as a kitchenette in a secondary dwelling. Modern single-wall designs in Eltham incorporate integrated appliances, floor-to-ceiling cabinetry for maximum storage and under-cabinet lighting to create depth and visual interest.

The best kitchen layout for your Eltham home ultimately depends on your available space, your family's lifestyle and how you use your kitchen day to day. A family that cooks elaborate meals needs a different layout to one that primarily reheats and entertains. Our team at Kitchen Renovations Eltham can help you explore all the possibilities during a free in-showroom consultation. We will walk you through full-size displays, discuss your specific needs and recommend a layout that makes the most of your Eltham kitchen. Visit us at 3 Bridge St, Eltham or call (03) 9989 6279 to start planning your perfect kitchen layout today.

blogPosts.title: How to Choose the Perfect Benchtop for Your Eltham Kitchen
blogPosts.excerpt: Choosing the right benchtop is critical to your Eltham kitchen renovation. Compare stone, laminate, timber and more to find the perfect match.
body: Your benchtop is the centrepiece of your kitchen, and choosing the right material is one of the most important decisions in any Eltham kitchen renovation. The benchtop sets the tone for the entire room, influences your daily workflow and needs to withstand years of cooking, entertaining and family life. Eltham homeowners have access to a wide range of benchtop materials, each with its own look, feel, durability profile and price point. From natural stone and engineered quartz to timber, laminate and concrete, the options can feel overwhelming. In this guide, we break down the pros and cons of the most popular benchtop materials available to Eltham renovators, helping you make a confident choice that suits your style, your budget and your lifestyle.

Caesarstone and engineered quartz have become the most popular benchtop choice for Eltham kitchen renovations, and for good reason. These engineered surfaces offer the luxurious look of natural stone without the ongoing maintenance requirements. Caesarstone is non-porous, meaning it resists stains from wine, coffee and cooking oils without the need for regular sealing. It is also highly scratch-resistant and available in an enormous range of colours and patterns, from classic whites to dramatic marbled designs. For Eltham families who want a benchtop that looks stunning and handles the rigours of daily use, Caesarstone is hard to beat. Pricing typically starts from around $450 per square metre installed, making it a mid-range option that delivers premium results. Our Eltham showroom has an extensive Caesarstone sample wall for you to explore.

Natural stone benchtops, including granite and marble, bring an unmatched sense of luxury and character to Eltham kitchens. Each slab of natural stone is unique, with its own colour variations, veining patterns and textural qualities that cannot be replicated by engineered materials. Granite is exceptionally durable and heat-resistant, making it an excellent choice for busy Eltham kitchens where hot pots and pans are a daily occurrence. Marble, while undeniably beautiful, is softer and more porous than granite, requiring regular sealing and more careful maintenance to prevent staining and etching. For Eltham homeowners who prioritise timeless beauty and are happy to invest in upkeep, natural stone is a wonderful choice. Prices for natural stone benchtops in Eltham typically range from $500 to $1,000 per square metre installed, depending on the stone variety and edge profile you select.

Timber benchtops offer warmth, natural beauty and a tactile quality that is perfect for Eltham's leafy, nature-inspired aesthetic. Hardwoods like Victorian ash, blackbutt and spotted gum are popular choices, each offering distinct grain patterns and colour tones. A timber benchtop develops a beautiful patina over time, gaining character and charm as it ages. However, timber does require more maintenance than stone or engineered surfaces. Regular oiling is necessary to protect the wood from moisture damage, and timber is more susceptible to scratches and heat marks. For Eltham homeowners who love the organic look of natural timber and are comfortable with ongoing care, a hardwood benchtop creates a kitchen that feels warm, inviting and uniquely yours. Timber benchtops typically cost between $300 and $600 per square metre installed.

Laminate benchtops remain a practical and affordable choice for Eltham kitchen renovations, particularly for budget-conscious renovators or investment properties. Modern laminates have come a long way, with many designs convincingly replicating the look of stone, timber and concrete at a fraction of the cost. Brands like Formica and Laminex offer hundreds of patterns and colours, including textures that mimic the feel of natural materials. Laminate is easy to clean, resistant to most stains and requires virtually no maintenance beyond regular wiping. The main drawback is that laminate is more susceptible to heat damage and chipping at the edges compared to stone or solid surface materials. For Eltham homeowners seeking an economical refresh, laminate benchtops start from around $150 per square metre installed, making them one of the most budget-friendly options available.

Choosing the right benchtop for your Eltham kitchen comes down to balancing aesthetics, durability, maintenance requirements and budget. There is no single best option, only the option that works best for your particular kitchen and lifestyle. The team at Kitchen Renovations Eltham can help you compare materials side by side in our Bridge St showroom, where you can see, touch and feel full-size samples of every benchtop material we offer. We will discuss your cooking habits, your family's needs and your renovation budget to recommend the benchtop that will serve you best for years to come. Visit us at 3 Bridge St, Eltham VIC 3095 or call (03) 9989 6279 to start your benchtop selection journey today.

blogPosts.title: How Long Does a Kitchen Renovation Take in Eltham?
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering how long your Eltham kitchen renovation will take? Here is a realistic timeline from planning to final walkthrough, with tips to keep your project on track.
body: One of the most common questions we hear from Eltham homeowners is how long a kitchen renovation will take from start to finish. The answer depends on the scope of your project, the complexity of the design and whether any structural changes are involved. A simple cosmetic refresh might be completed in as little as two to three weeks, while a full structural renovation involving new plumbing, electrical work and custom cabinetry can take anywhere from eight to twelve weeks or longer. Eltham's unique housing stock, from period homes with original plumbing to modern builds with complex electrical requirements, means every project has its own timeline. Understanding the typical stages of a kitchen renovation will help you plan around the disruption and keep your Eltham household running smoothly.

The planning and design phase is the first stage of your Eltham kitchen renovation and typically takes two to four weeks. This is when we work with you to finalise your kitchen layout, select materials, choose colours and confirm all specifications. Visiting our Eltham showroom at 3 Bridge St allows you to see and touch materials in person, which helps speed up decision-making significantly. During this phase, we also prepare detailed plans, submit any required council applications for heritage properties and place orders for materials and appliances. Getting this stage right is critical, because changes made after construction begins can cause costly delays. Our experienced Eltham design team will guide you through every decision, ensuring your renovation plan is complete and accurate before any demolition work commences.

The demolition and structural work phase usually takes one to two weeks and is the most disruptive part of your Eltham kitchen renovation. During this stage, existing cabinetry, benchtops, splashbacks and sometimes flooring are removed. If your renovation involves moving walls, relocating plumbing or upgrading electrical wiring, this work happens now. Eltham homeowners should prepare a temporary kitchen in another room with essential appliances like a microwave, toaster and kettle to maintain some normalcy during this period. Our team takes care to minimise dust and disruption, sealing off the work area from the rest of your home. For Eltham homes built before the 1990s, there is also the possibility of encountering asbestos or outdated wiring that requires specialist removal, so it is wise to factor additional time into your project schedule.

The installation phase is where your new Eltham kitchen truly comes to life, and this typically takes three to five weeks. New plumbing and electrical connections are completed first, followed by the installation of custom cabinetry, benchtops, splashbacks and appliances. This stage requires careful coordination between multiple trades, including plumbers, electricians, cabinet makers and stonemasons. Our Kitchen Renovations Eltham team manages all scheduling and logistics, ensuring each trade arrives at the right time and that work progresses smoothly. Benchtop fabrication usually takes one to two weeks after the final template measurement, so there may be a short pause between cabinetry installation and benchtop fitting. Throughout this phase, our project manager keeps you updated on progress and any decisions that need your input.

The final finishing and handover stage takes approximately one week and covers all the detail work that makes your new Eltham kitchen truly complete. This includes installing handles and hardware, completing any touch-up painting, fitting kickboards and completing final plumbing connections such as the sink and dishwasher. A thorough clean of the entire kitchen and surrounding areas is included. Our team then conducts a detailed walkthrough with you, inspecting every element of the renovation to ensure it meets our exacting standards and your expectations. Any items on the defects or adjustments list are addressed promptly. For Eltham homeowners, this final stage is exciting because it is when you see your dream kitchen fully realised for the first time, ready to be enjoyed every day.

To keep your Eltham kitchen renovation on schedule, clear communication and timely decision-making are essential. Delays in material selections, appliance deliveries or change requests during construction are the most common causes of project overruns. Our team at Kitchen Renovations Eltham provides a detailed project timeline at the start of your renovation so you know exactly what to expect and when. We also maintain regular communication throughout the project, keeping you informed of progress and flagging any potential issues early. If you are planning a kitchen renovation in Eltham and want a realistic timeline for your specific project, visit our showroom at 3 Bridge St or call (03) 9989 6279 for a free consultation and detailed project schedule.
